batch: B is the number of logical requests circulating in the closed batch. M is the number of requests per microbatch. PP is the number of pipeline stages. Simultaneously executing requests are not the full denominator of user throughput.
steady_equal_length_rule: For a stable closed batch whose B requests generate at approximately the same rate over the same measurement window, aggregate decode tok/s divided by B approximates each user's decode rate. Individual measured intervals and the distribution remain authoritative.

PP2_B16_M4_example.interpretation: 60/8=7.5 counts only the8 currently computing users and omits waiting for the other two microbatches. If B is actually reduced to8 and measured total remains60, then7.5/user is valid; unchanged total is not guaranteed.

actual_latest_Kimi_N4_configuration.difference: Actual per-request windows are not exactly the aggregate window; first-ready-to-last-ready also retains waiting while other cohorts still prefill. Neither metric is HTTP client delivery speed.

15_user_target.hardware_reachability: Not yet proved; achieved large-GEMM/read benchmarks are references, not physical peaks or a small-M inference roof. No physical maximum TPS or15/user achieved claim.
